Language Lab

There is / There are: What's in the House

Amanda Foster · your guide for this lab

Hi again! This time we're talking about things, not actions. When we say what's in a place, English uses "there is" and "there are". Let's look at the pattern, and then, the #1 trap I see with Portuguese speakers.

How it works

There is + a/an + singular noun
There are + plural noun
  • There is a sofa in the living room.Há um sofá na sala.
  • There are two stools at the island.Há dois banquinhos na ilha.
  • There is a rug under the table.Há um tapete debaixo da mesa.
  • There are plants on the shelf.Há plantas na prateleira.

Your turn: Talk · Info Gap

Play with a partner. Don't show your partner the picture! Student A looks at the Living Room. Student B looks at the Kitchen. Ask each other questions and draw what your partner describes.

Is there a plant? How many chairs are there? Is there a rug on the floor? What color is the sofa? Where is the lamp?
